court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals

issues.label: Rehabilitation's role in eligibility analysis
issues.why: The court must decide whether rehabilitation may count toward extraordinary and compelling reasons or is limited to non-dangerousness.

issues.label: Holistic vs. piecemeal factor evaluation
issues.why: The court must determine whether factors are assessed collectively or each must individually be extraordinary and compelling.

issues.label: Statutory interpretation of catch-all (a)(3)
issues.why: The scope of 'other extraordinary and compelling reasons' and whether its listed examples are non-exhaustive must be construed.

issues.label: Whether (a)(3) examples are exhaustive
issues.why: Court must decide if factors outside the four enumerated illustrations can qualify under the catch-all.

issues.label: Age below sixty as partial factor
issues.why: Court must decide whether sub-sixty age can contribute to eligibility despite the categorical sixty-year threshold.

issues.label: Effect of federal statute divergence
issues.why: The District's omission of the federal rehabilitation-alone bar and other differences affects how the statute should be interpreted.

issues.label: Relevance of § 994(t) rehabilitation-alone bar
issues.why: Whether the federal prohibition on rehabilitation-alone applies given the District statute's silence must be resolved.

issues.label: COVID-19 vulnerability finding review
issues.why: Court's determination that Allen lacked acute vulnerability to severe COVID-19 outcomes must be assessed.

issues.label: Standard of review on statutory interpretation
issues.why: Interpretation of the statute is de novo while factual findings warrant deference.

issues.label: Standard of review on eligibility factual findings
issues.why: The applicable deference for the court's factual eligibility determinations must be identified.

issues.label: Weight of debilitating medical condition
issues.why: Whether Allen's comorbidities constitute a qualifying debilitating or serious medical condition must be evaluated.

issues.label: Movant's burden of proof
issues.why: The court must apply the correct allocation and standard of proof for demonstrating extraordinary and compelling reasons.

issues.label: Legislative history and remedial purpose
issues.why: The COVID-era enactment and remedial intent may inform broad construction of the statute.

issues.label: Length of incarceration as factor
issues.why: Whether twenty-plus years served can be weighed toward eligibility outside the categorical criteria must be decided.

issues.label: Interaction of non-dangerousness and eligibility
issues.why: Court must clarify whether the two requirements are analytically distinct and whether evidence can serve both.

issues.label: Consideration of victim-impact statements
issues.why: How victim opposition factors into eligibility versus dangerousness must be addressed.

issues.label: Remedy if legal error found
issues.why: Court must determine whether to remand for reconsideration under the correct standard or decide eligibility itself.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: Even if the trial court erred legally, whether the error affected the outcome must be considered.

issues.label: Mandatory nature of relief once requirements met
issues.why: The 'shall modify' language means eligibility plus non-dangerousness compels release, affecting the stakes of the analysis.

issues.label: Application of §§ 3142(g) and 3553(a) factors
issues.why: The statute's incorporation of these factors and their proper role in the analysis must be considered.
